# ExKnowledge

> Practical explosion protection reference for engineers. ATEX, IECEx, zone classification, gas groups, temperature classes, protection methods, certification.

ExKnowledge covers the technical fundamentals of explosion protection (Ex) for hazardous areas. Written for engineers, technical sales, and anyone working with certified equipment in explosive atmospheres.

## Topics

- [Fundamentals](https://exknowledge.com/pages/fundamentals.html): Fire triangle, explosive atmospheres, LEL/UEL, 13 ignition sources, three protection principles
- [Zone Classification](https://exknowledge.com/pages/zone-classification.html): Zones 0/1/2 (gas), Zones 20/21/22 (dust), IEC 60079-10 methodology
- [Gas Groups](https://exknowledge.com/pages/gas-groups.html): IIA/IIB/IIC, MESG, MIC ratio, dust groups IIIA/IIIB/IIIC, NEC equivalents
- [Temperature Classes](https://exknowledge.com/pages/temperature-classes.html): T1-T6, auto-ignition temperatures, dust layer ignition
- [Protection Methods](https://exknowledge.com/pages/protection-methods.html): Ex d, Ex e, Ex i, Ex p, Ex n, Ex m, Ex o, Ex q, Ex t, Ex Op with zone suitability matrix
- [Equipment Protection Levels](https://exknowledge.com/pages/epl.html): Ga/Gb/Gc, Da/Db/Dc, ATEX category mapping
- [Ex Markings](https://exknowledge.com/pages/ex-markings.html): How to read ATEX/IECEx equipment labels, 5 real examples
- [Standards](https://exknowledge.com/pages/standards.html): IEC 60079 series, ATEX 2014/34/EU, 1999/92/EC, NEC 500/505, regional standards
- [Certification](https://exknowledge.com/pages/certification.html): Notified Bodies, IECEx scheme, ExTR, quality systems, CompEx
- [Installation & Inspection](https://exknowledge.com/pages/installation-inspection.html): IEC 60079-14, 60079-17, cable glands, inspection grades, common errors
- [Cheat Sheet](https://exknowledge.com/pages/cheat-sheet.html): Quick qualification questions, zone-EPL mapping, decision tree, cost/timeline
- [FAQ](https://exknowledge.com/pages/faq.html): Frequently asked questions about ATEX, IECEx, zone classification, Ex markings, certification

## In-Depth Guides

- [ATEX vs IECEx](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-vs-iecex.html): Geographic scope, legal basis, marking differences, mutual recognition
- [NEC 500/505 vs ATEX/IECEx](https://exknowledge.com/pages/nec-500-vs-atex-iec.html): North American Class/Division vs international Zone system, conversion tables, dual-certified equipment, multinational facilities
- [DSEAR Regulations (UK)](https://exknowledge.com/pages/dsear-regulations-uk.html): UK Dangerous Substances and Explosive Atmospheres Regulations 2002, employer duties, risk assessment, ATEX relationship post-Brexit, HSE enforcement
- [ATEX Equipment Categories 1, 2, 3](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-equipment-categories.html): Category 1/2/3 for Group II, M1/M2 for mining, zone mapping, EPL relationship, conformity assessment modules, practical selection examples
- [Explosion Proof vs Intrinsically Safe](https://exknowledge.com/pages/explosion-proof-vs-intrinsically-safe.html): Ex d vs Ex i comparison — cost, size, maintenance, zone suitability
- [How to Read an ATEX Nameplate](https://exknowledge.com/pages/how-to-read-atex-nameplate.html): 6 annotated real-world examples, complete decoding methodology
- [ATEX Directive 2014/34/EU](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-directive.html): Regulatory guide, conformity assessment modules, manufacturer obligations
- [Hazardous Area Classification](https://exknowledge.com/pages/hazardous-area-classification.html): IEC 60079-10 methodology, source of release, ventilation assessment
- [Dust Explosion Protection](https://exknowledge.com/pages/dust-explosion-protection.html): Zone 20/21/22, dust characteristics, Kst values, case studies
- [ATEX for Beginners](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-for-beginners.html): Plain-language introduction to explosion protection concepts
- [CompEx Certification Guide](https://exknowledge.com/pages/compex-certification.html): Training units, exam structure, career benefits, renewal
- [Hydrogen Explosion Protection](https://exknowledge.com/pages/hydrogen-explosion-protection.html): IIC challenges, TPRD venting, electrolysis facilities, infrastructure scaling
- [Cable Glands for Hazardous Areas](https://exknowledge.com/pages/cable-glands-hazardous-areas.html): Barrier vs non-barrier, flameproof, selection criteria, installation
- [Ex Equipment Selection Guide](https://exknowledge.com/pages/ex-equipment-selection-guide.html): Step-by-step methodology from zone classification to procurement

## Tools

- [Ex Certificate Scanner](https://exknowledge.com/exscanner/): Upload ATEX/IECEx certificate PDFs — extracts equipment marking, gas group, temperature class, protection type. 100% client-side, privacy-first.
- [Multilingual Ex Glossary](https://exknowledge.com/glossary/): 77 official Ex/ATEX/IECEx terms translated across 19 languages. Sourced from IEC 60079, national standards bodies, and IECEx member institutes. Search, compare, and download.

## Glossary Terms (77 terms, 19 languages)

The full multilingual glossary covers official Ex terminology in: English, Norwegian, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Danish, Finnish, Swedish, Polish, Czech, Russian, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Turkish, Arabic.

Key terms include: ambient temperature, area classification, ATEX certification, auto-ignition temperature, cable gland, category (ATEX), CE marking, certification body, clearances and creepage distances, competent person, conformity assessment, dust explosion, dust ignition-proof, encapsulation (Ex m), EPL (Equipment Protection Level), equipment group, Ex marking, explosion group, explosion proof (Ex d), explosive atmosphere, flame arrester, flameproof enclosure, gas detector, gas group, Group I, Group II, Group III, hazardous area, IEC 60079, IECEx, ignition source, increased safety (Ex e), inspection, installation, instrinsic safety (Ex i), IP rating, maximum surface temperature, MESG, minimum ignition current, minimum ignition energy, non-incendive (Ex n), notified body, oil immersion (Ex o), operating temperature, permit to work, powder filling (Ex q), pressurization (Ex p), protection concept, protection level, quality system, safe area, special protection (Ex s), T-rating, temperature class, type of protection, zone 0, zone 1, zone 2, zone 20, zone 21, zone 22.

## Site Technical Details

- Static site hosted on GitHub Pages
- 299 pages across 11 languages
- Schema.org structured data (Article, BlogPosting, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage)
- All content based on IEC 60079, ATEX 2014/34/EU, IECEx standards
- Not a substitute for official standards documents or professional engineering advice

## NEC 500/505 vs ATEX/IECEx
- URL: https://exknowledge.com/pages/nec-500-vs-atex-iec.html
- Complete comparison of NEC 500 Class/Division and NEC 505 Zone systems versus ATEX and IECEx
- Covers: Division-to-Zone mapping, gas group cross-reference, protection method equivalencies, dual certification, multinational facility guidance

## DSEAR Regulations (UK)
- URL: https://exknowledge.com/pages/dsear-regulations-uk.html
- UK Dangerous Substances and Explosive Atmospheres Regulations 2002
- Covers: employer duties, risk assessment steps, DSEAR vs ATEX post-Brexit, zone classification, enforcement and penalties

## ATEX Equipment Categories
- URL: https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-equipment-categories.html
- ATEX equipment categories 1, 2, 3 for Group II (surface industries) and M1, M2 for Group I (mining)
- Covers: category-to-zone mapping, EPL relationship, fault tolerance, practical selection examples, common mistakes

## New guides (September 2026)
- Does it need ATEX zoning? Hazardous area classification by application: https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-applications.html — A practical test for when a site needs ATEX zoning, with quick answers for battery rooms, EV charging, electrolysers, CO2, spray booths, silos and more.
- Battery rooms and battery energy storage: do they need ATEX zoning?: https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-battery-rooms.html — Do battery charging rooms need ATEX zones? How IEC 62485 ventilation keeps hydrogen below 4 %, when a zone remains, and how NFPA 855 treats lithium-ion BESS.
- EV charging and hazardous areas: petrol stations, car parks and ATEX: https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-ev-charging.html — Do EV chargers need ATEX zoning? Not in car parks. At petrol stations the charger, vehicle and cable must sit outside the forecourt hazardous areas (UK and US).
- Hydrogen electrolysers: ATEX zoning and hazardous area classification: https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-hydrogen-electrolysers.html — How hydrogen electrolyser containers and rooms are zoned: IEC 60079-10-1 release sources, ventilation and Zone 2 NE, IIC equipment, vents and the oxygen side.
- Does CO2 need an ATEX zone?: https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-co2.html — CO2 is not flammable, so it never creates an ATEX zone. What CO2 areas need instead, and when breweries, CCS plants or inerted vessels still need zoning.
- Do Paint Spray Booths Need ATEX Zoning? Zones, Interlocks and Equipment: https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-spray-booths.html — Do paint spray booths need ATEX zoning? Yes. How zones are set inside booths, ducts and around openings under EN 16985, DSEAR and NFPA 33, plus powder booths.
- Do Grain Silos, Flour Mills and Feed Mills Need ATEX Zoning?: https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-grain-silos-flour-mills.html — Grain, flour and feed dust is combustible. How Zones 20, 21 and 22 are set in silos, elevators and mills, why housekeeping matters, and OSHA and NFPA 660 rules.
- Do Biogas and Anaerobic Digestion Plants Need ATEX Zoning?: https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-biogas-plants.html — Biogas plants need hazardous area classification: methane and H2S data, zones around digesters, relief valves, condensate traps and CHP rooms, and TRGS 529.
- Do Distilleries Need ATEX Zoning? Whisky, Gin and Ethanol Plants: https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-distilleries.html — Do distilleries need ATEX zoning? Usually yes. Ethanol data, zones around stills, receivers, cask filling, warehouses and malt mills, and DSEAR and US rules.
- Ex Certification by Country: ATEX, IECEx, UKCA and National Schemes Compared: https://exknowledge.com/pages/ex-certification-schemes.html — Compare Ex certification schemes by country: ATEX, IECEx, UKCA, NEC/CEC, INMETRO, CCC, KCs, Japan, PESO, EAC and ANZEx, with IECEx use and local rules.
- UKCA Ex (UKEX) Certification: Equipment for Explosive Atmospheres in the UK: https://exknowledge.com/pages/ukca-ex-certification.html — UKCA/UKEX for Ex equipment under the 2016 Regulations: approved vs notified bodies, marking, CE recognized in GB indefinitely, Northern Ireland and DSEAR.
- EAC Ex Certification for the Eurasian Economic Union (TR CU 012/2011): https://exknowledge.com/pages/eac-ex-certification.html — EAC Ex certification under TR CU 012/2011 for the Eurasian Economic Union: schemes, local applicant, accredited bodies, GOST standards, Ex and EAC marking.
- India: PESO Approval for Ex Equipment in Hazardous Areas: https://exknowledge.com/pages/india-peso-ex-certification.html — How PESO approves Ex electrical equipment in India under the Petroleum Rules 2002: IECEx and EU routes, Indian applicant, recognized labs, BIS and marking.
- China CCC Ex Certification for Explosion-Protected Equipment: https://exknowledge.com/pages/china-ccc-ex-certification.html — Since October 2020 Ex electrical products sold in China need CCC. Scope, designated bodies such as NEPSI and CNEx, GB/T 3836, IECEx use and marking.
- South Korea KCs Ex Certification for Explosion-Protected Equipment: https://exknowledge.com/pages/korea-kcs-ex-certification.html — Ex electrical equipment sold in South Korea needs KCs safety certification from KOSHA, KTL or KGS. IECEx route, agent rules, reviews and KCs marking.
- Japan Ex Certification: Type Examination of Explosion-Protected Electrical Equipment: https://exknowledge.com/pages/japan-jpex-ex-certification.html — Ex electrical equipment for Japan needs type examination by an MHLW-registered body. Two routes, IECEx ExTR use, the 8 bodies, 3-year validity, marking.
- Intrinsic Safety Loop Calculator: https://exknowledge.com/pages/intrinsic-safety-calculator.html — Free intrinsic safety loop calculator: check Uo, Io, Po, Co and Lo against Ui, Ii, Pi, Ci, Li and cable per IEC 60079-14, with the 1 % mixed-circuit rule.
- Ex Industry Monthly July 2026: https://exknowledge.com/blog/2026-07.html
- Ex Industry Monthly September 2026: https://exknowledge.com/blog/2026-09.html
